repoMeta.name: express
repoMeta.description: Fast, unopinionated, minimalist web framework for node.

summary: Express 5 is a thin HTTP framework on top of Node's http module. createApplication() returns a request handler function with the application prototype mixed in; per-request it swaps the prototypes of Node's req/res for Express's extended versions and delegates routing to the separate `router` package. Settings (trust proxy, query parser, etag, view cache) are compiled into functions by utils.js, and views are resolved and rendered by the View class.

nodes.label: createApplication()
nodes.summary: Package entry. index.js re-exports lib/express.js, which builds `app` as a (req, res, next) function, mixes in EventEmitter and the application prototype, creates per-app request/response prototypes and re-exports Router, json/urlencoded/raw/text and static middleware.

nodes.label: Application Core
nodes.summary: The app prototype: settings store and inheritance on mount, lazily created router, app.handle (sets X-Powered-By, swaps req/res prototypes, hands off to the router), app.use mounting of middleware and sub-apps, app.render with the view cache, and app.listen.

nodes.label: Router (external package)
nodes.summary: Routing moved out of core in Express 5: the `router` package matches paths, runs the middleware stack and route handlers. Express only instantiates it (app.router getter) and forwards app.use / app.route / app.param / app[method] to it.

nodes.label: Request Extensions
nodes.summary: Prototype layered over http.IncomingMessage: content negotiation (accepts*), req.is, and lazy getters such as query, protocol, secure, ip/ips, hostname, subdomains and fresh/stale — the proxy-aware ones consult the compiled 'trust proxy fn'.

nodes.label: Response Helpers
nodes.summary: Prototype layered over http.ServerResponse: status, send (ETag + freshness), json/jsonp, sendFile/download via `send`, format, cookie/clearCookie, location/redirect and render (which delegates to app.render).

nodes.label: View Resolution
nodes.summary: View resolves a template name against one or more view roots (trying <name>.<ext> and <name>/index.<ext>), auto-loads an engine by requiring the module named after the extension, and forces engine callbacks to be async.

nodes.label: Settings Compilers & Utils
nodes.summary: Turns settings into functions: compileETag (weak/strong), compileQueryParser (simple via node:querystring, extended via qs), compileTrust (proxy-addr); plus content-type helpers and the list of HTTP methods used to generate app.get/app.post/….

nodes.label: Examples
nodes.summary: Runnable sample apps (auth, mvc, error-pages, route-map, …). The MVC example auto-mounts controllers that use a fake in-memory db.

nodes.label: Package & CI
nodes.summary: package.json (Node ≥ 18, dependencies on router, body-parser, send, serve-static…), lint config and GitHub workflows for CI and CodeQL.

bugs.title: Extended query parser lets query keys shadow Object.prototype
bugs.description: When an app opts into `app.set('query parser', 'extended')`, parsing uses qs with `allowPrototypes: true`. A request like `?hasOwnProperty=x` or `?toString=1` then overwrites those methods on req.query, and handler code such as `req.query.hasOwnProperty('page')` throws a TypeError. Any client can trigger that 500. The default parser is 'simple' (application.js line 97), so only opted-in apps are exposed.
bugs.suggestedFix: Drop `allowPrototypes: true` (qs then ignores keys that collide with prototype properties), or parse into a null-prototype object with `plainObjects: true`. Note the change in the 5.x release notes.

bugs.title: MVC example controllers crash on malformed form bodies
bugs.description: create() reads `body.pet.name` without checking that `body.pet` exists, so a POST without that field throws a TypeError and returns 500. user/index.js (line 38) and pet/index.js (line 28) repeat the pattern. Example code gets copied into real apps, so this teaches an unsafe habit, and it also stores an empty or oversized pet name unchecked.
bugs.suggestedFix: Validate before use: `if (!body.pet || typeof body.pet.name !== 'string' || !body.pet.name.trim()) return res.status(400).send('Pet name required')`. Apply the same guard in the user and pet controllers.

bugs.title: req.query re-parses on every access, so mutations are lost
bugs.description: In Express 5, req.query is a getter that calls the query parser on every read and returns a fresh object. Middleware that normalizes values in place (`req.query.page = Number(req.query.page)`) silently has no effect on later reads, and handlers that read req.query repeatedly re-parse the URL each time.
bugs.suggestedFix: Memoize the parsed object per request (cache it on a symbol, keyed by req.url) so repeated reads are cheap and consistent. Alternatively, document that req.query is read-only and point users to res.locals for derived values.

bugs.title: View extension decides which module gets require()'d
bugs.description: When no engine is registered for a view's extension, View does `require(this.ext.slice(1)).__express`. If an app passes user-influenced names to res.render (for example `res.render(req.params.page)`), the request controls which installed package is loaded and invoked as a template engine. The `__express` check limits this to real engines, but it still widens the attack surface and lets unexpected engines execute templates.
bugs.suggestedFix: Register engines explicitly via app.engine() at startup and add an opt-out setting such as `app.set('view engine autoload', false)` that makes unknown extensions throw instead of require()-ing.

bugs.title: X-Powered-By: Express is sent by default
bugs.description: defaultConfiguration() enables 'x-powered-by', and app.handle (lines 160-162) adds the header to every response. It advertises the framework to scanners for no functional benefit, and many security checklists flag it.
bugs.suggestedFix: Keep the default for compatibility but call it out in the security best-practices docs (`app.disable('x-powered-by')`), or flip the default in the next major version.

bugs.title: Uncached view lookups block the event loop with statSync
bugs.description: View.resolve calls tryStat, which uses fs.statSync up to twice per root for every render. 'view cache' is enabled only when NODE_ENV === 'production' (application.js lines 138-140), so staging environments that forget NODE_ENV do synchronous filesystem I/O on the request path.
bugs.suggestedFix: Use fs.promises.stat in an async lookup path (View.render is already callback-based), or log a startup warning when 'view cache' is disabled outside development.

walkthrough.title: Start here: what Express 5 depends on
walkthrough.explanation: Skim package.json first. In Express 5, much of the behavior lives in dependencies: routing is the `router` package, and parsing comes from body-parser and serve-static. Knowing that tells you which bugs belong in this repo and which belong upstream.

walkthrough.title: Entry point: an app is just a function
walkthrough.explanation: lib/express.js creates `app` as a plain (req, res, next) function, mixes in EventEmitter and the application prototype, and builds request/response prototypes that point back to the app. That's why you can pass an Express app directly to http.createServer.

walkthrough.title: Core logic: settings, mounting and app.handle
walkthrough.explanation: Read app.init/defaultConfiguration for the default settings, then app.handle: it sets X-Powered-By, swaps the prototypes of Node's req/res, creates res.locals and hands off to the router. app.use shows how sub-apps inherit settings on 'mount'.

walkthrough.title: The request/response surface
walkthrough.explanation: Most of what users touch lives in these two prototypes. Note how proxy-aware getters (protocol, ip, hostname) only trust X-Forwarded-* headers when the compiled 'trust proxy fn' allows it.

walkthrough.title: Settings become functions
walkthrough.explanation: utils.js turns declarative settings into the functions used at request time: compileTrust → proxy-addr, compileQueryParser → querystring or qs, compileETag → etag. This is where a setting change actually alters runtime behavior.

walkthrough.title: Good first contribution: harden the MVC example
walkthrough.explanation: The MVC example controllers dereference req.body fields without checks, so malformed POSTs crash with a 500. Adding input validation and a 400 response in the three controllers is a contained, reviewable first PR that improves code people copy.
